q: A boat can travel with a speed of 13 km/hr in still water. If the speed of the stream is 4 km/hr, find the time taken by the boat to go 68 km downstream.
s: Speed downstream = (13 + 4) km/hr = 17 km/hr Time taken to travel 68 km downstream = $$\frac{{68}}{{17}}$$ hours = 4 hours

q: A man's speed with the current is 15 km/hr and the speed of the current is 2.5 km/hr. The man's speed against the current is:
s: Man's rate in still water = (15 - 2.5) km/hr = 12.5 km/hr. Man's rate against the current = (12.5 - 2.5) km/hr = 10 km/hr.

q: A boat running upstream takes 8 hours 48 minutes to cover a certain distance, while it takes 4 hours to cover the same distance running downstream. What is the ratio between the speed of the boat and speed of the water current respectively?
s: Let the man's rate upstream be x kmph and that downstream be y kmph. Then, distance covered upstream in 8 hrs 48 min = Distance covered downstream in 4 hrs. $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow {x \times 8\frac{4}{5}} = {y \times 4} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{44}}{5}x = 4y \\ & \Rightarrow y = \frac{{11}}{5}x \\ & \therefore {\text{Required}}\,{\text{ratio}} \\ & = {\frac{{y + x}}{2}} : {\frac{{y - x}}{2}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{16x}}{5} \times \frac{1}{2}} \right):\left( {\frac{{6x}}{5} \times \frac{1}{2}} \right) \\ & = \frac{8}{5}:\frac{3}{5} \\ & = 8:3 \end{aligned}$$

q: A motorboat, whose speed in 15 km/hr in still water goes 30 km downstream and comes back in a total of 4 hours 30 minutes. The speed of the stream (in km/hr) is:
s: Let the speed of the stream be x km/hr Then, Speed downstream = (15 + x) km/hr Speed upstream = (15 - x) km/hr $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{{30}}{{ {15 + x} }} + \frac{{30}}{{ {15 - x} }} = 4\frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{900}}{{225 - {x^2}}} = \frac{9}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow 9{x^2} = 225 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} = 25 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 5\,km/hr \end{aligned}$$

q: In one hour, a boat goes 11 km/hr along the stream and 5 km/hr against the stream. The speed of the boat in still water (in km/hr) is:
s: Speed in still water = $$\frac{1}{2}$$(11 + 5) kmph = 8 kmph

q: A boat running downstream covers a distance of 16 km in 2 hours while for covering the same distance upstream, it takes 4 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
s: Rate downstream = $$\frac{{16}}{2}$$ kmph = 8 kmph Rate upstream = $$\frac{{16}}{4}$$ kmph = 4 kmph ∴ Speed in still water = $$\frac{1}{2}$$(8 + 4) kmph = 6 kmph

q: The speed of a boat in still water in 15 km/hr and the rate of current is 3 km/hr. The distance travelled downstream in 12 minutes is:
s: Speed downstream = (15 + 3) kmph = 18 kmph Distance travelled = $$\left( {18 \times \frac{{12}}{{60}}} \right)$$ km = 3.6 km

q: A boat takes 90 minutes less to travel 36 miles downstream than to travel the same distance upstream. If the speed of the boat in still water is 10 mph, the speed of the stream is:
s: Let the speed of the stream x mph. Then, Speed downstream = (10 + x) mph Speed upstream = (10 - x) mph $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{{36}}{{ {10 - x} }} - \frac{{36}}{{ {10 + x} }} = \frac{{90}}{{60}} \\ & \Rightarrow 72x \times 60 = 90\left( {100 - {x^2}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} + 48x - 100 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {x + 50} \right)\left( {x - 2} \right) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 2\,\text{mph} \end{aligned}$$

q: A man can row at 5 kmph in still water. If the velocity of current is 1 kmph and it takes him 1 hour to row to a place and come back, how far is the place?
s: Speed downstream = (5 + 1) kmph = 6 kmph Speed upstream = (5 - 1) kmph = 4 kmph Let the required distance be x km Then, $$\frac{x}{6} + \frac{x}{4}$$ = 1 ⇒ 2x + 3x = 12 ⇒ 5x = 12 ⇒ x = 2.4 km

q: A boat covers a certain distance downstream in 1 hour, while it comes back in $$1\frac{1}{2}$$ hours. If the speed of the stream be 3 kmph, what is the speed of the boat in still water?
s: Let the speed of the boat in still water be x kmph Then Speed downstream = (x + 3) kmph Speed upstream = (x - 3) kmph $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \left( {x + 3} \right) \times 1 = \left( {x - 3} \right) \times \frac{3}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow 2x + 6 = 3x - 9 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 15\,\text{kmph} \end{aligned}$$

q: A boatman goes 2 km against the current of the stream in 1 hour and goes 1 km along the current in 10 minutes. How long will it take to go 5 km in stationary water?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Rate}}\,{\text{downstream}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{1}{{10}} \times 60} \right)km/hr = 6\,km/hr \\ & {\text{Rate}}\,{\text{upstream}} = 2\,km/hr \\ & {\text{Speed}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{still}}\,{\text{water}} \\ & = \frac{1}{2}\left( {6 + 2} \right)km/hr = 4\,km/hr \\ & \therefore {\text{Required}}\,{\text{time}} \\ & = {\frac{5}{4}} \,hrs \\ & = 1\frac{1}{4}hrs \\ & = 1\,hr\,15\,\min . \end{aligned}$$

q: A man can row three-quarters of a kilometer against the stream in $$11\frac{1}{4}$$ minutes and down the stream in $$7\frac{1}{2}$$ minutes. The speed (in km/hr) of the man in still water is:
s: We can write three - quarters of a kilometer as 750 meters and $$11\frac{1}{4}$$ minutes as 675 seconds $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Rate}}\,{\text{upstream}} \\ & = {\frac{{750}}{{675}}} m/\sec = \frac{{10}}{9}m/\sec \\ & {\text{Rate}}\,{\text{downstream}} \\ & = {\frac{{750}}{{450}}} m/\sec = \frac{5}{3}m/\sec \\ & \therefore {\text{Rate}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{still}}\,{\text{water}} \\ & = \frac{1}{2}\left( {\frac{{10}}{9} + \frac{5}{3}} \right)m/\sec \\ & = \frac{{25}}{{18}}\,m/\sec \\ & = \left( {\frac{{25}}{{18}} \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \right)km/hr \\ & = 5\,km/hr \end{aligned}$$

q: Speed of a boat in standing water is 9 kmph and the speed of the stream is 1.5 kmph. A man rows to a place at a distance of 105 km and comes back to the starting point. The total time taken by him is:
s: Speed upstream = 7.5 kmph Speed downstream = 10.5 kmph ∴ Total time taken = $$\left( {\frac{{105}}{{7.5}} + \frac{{105}}{{10.5}}} \right)$$ hours = 24 hours

q: A man takes twice as long to row a distance against the stream as to row the same distance in favour of the stream. The ratio of the speed of the boat (in still water) and the stream is:
s: Let man's rate upstream be x kmph Then, his rate downstream = 2x kmph ∴ (speed in still water) : (Speed of stream) $$\begin{aligned} & = {\frac{{2x + x}}{2}} : {\frac{{2x - x}}{2}} \\ & = \frac{{3x}}{2}:\frac{x}{2} \\ & = 3:1 \end{aligned}$$

q: A man rows to a place 48 km distant and come back in 14 hours. He finds that he can row 4 km with the stream in the same time as 3 km against the stream. The rate of the stream is:
s: Suppose he move 4 km downstream in x hours Then, Speed downstream = $$\frac{4}{x}$$ km/hr Speed upstream = $$\frac{3}{x}$$ km/hr $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{{48}}{{\left( {4/x} \right)}} + \frac{{48}}{{\left( {3/x} \right)}} = 14\,or\,x = \frac{1}{2} \end{aligned}$$ So, Speed downstream = 8 km/hr Speed upstream = 6 km/hr ∴ Rate of the stream = $$\frac{1}{2}$$(8 - 6) km/hr = 1 km/hr

q: A man can row at a speed of $$4\frac{1}{2}$$ km/hr in still water. If he takes 2 times as long to row a distance upstream as to row the same distance downstream, then the speed of stream (in km/hr) is-
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed of man in still water , }} \\ & x{\text{ }} = {\text{ }}\frac{9}{2}km/hr{\text{ }} \\ & {\text{let speed of stream = }}y{\text{ }}km/h \\ & {\text{Downstream speed = }} {\frac{9}{2} + y} \\ & {\text{Upstream speed = }} {\frac{9}{2} - y} \\ & {\text{Accroding to questions,}} \\ & {\text{2}} \times {\frac{{{\text{Distance}}}}{{ {\frac{9}{2} + y} }}} = \frac{{{\text{Distance}}}}{{ {\frac{9}{2} - y} }} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{2}{{\frac{9}{2} + y}} = \frac{1}{{\frac{9}{2} - y}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{2 \times 2}}{{9 + 2y}} = \frac{2}{{9 - 2y}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{2}{{9 + 2y}} = \frac{1}{{9 - 2y}} \\ & \Rightarrow 18 - 4y = 9 + 2y \\ & \Rightarrow 6y = 9 \\ & \Rightarrow y = \frac{9}{6} = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5\,km/h \end{aligned}$$

q: A boat covers 24 km upstream and 36 km downstream in 6 hours, while it covers 36 km upstream and 24 km downstream in $$6\frac{1}{2}$$ hours. The speed of the current is?
s: let speed of boat in still water = x km/h Speed of stream current = y km/h According to question, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{24}}{{x - y}} + \frac{{36}}{{x + y}} = 6h\,......\,(i) \\ & \frac{{36}}{{x - y}} + \frac{{24}}{{x + y}} = \frac{{13}}{2}h\,......\,(ii) \end{aligned}$$ In these type of questions, make factor of 24 and 36 and choose the common values which satisfy the above equations. $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{24 = 2,3,4,6,8,}}\boxed{12} \\ & 36 = 3,4,9,\boxed{12} \end{aligned}$$ Choose the common factor i.e. Put this value in equation (i) $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{24}}{{x - y}} + \frac{{36}}{{12}} = 6 \\ & \frac{{24}}{{x - y}} + 3 = 6 \\ & x - y = 8 \\ & \therefore x + y = 12 \\ & \therefore x = 10\,\,\,,\,\,\,\,y = 2 \\ & {\text{Speed of the current,}} \\ & y = 2{\text{ km/h}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A boat while dowenstream in a reiver converd a distance of 50 miles at an average speed of 60 miles per hour. While returning , because of the water resistance , it took 1 hour 15 minutes to cover the same distance What was the average speed during the whole journey?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Time taken to cover 50 miles downstream}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{50}}{{60}}} \right)hr{\text{ = }}\frac{5}{6}hr.{\text{ }} \\ & {\text{Time taken to cover 50 miles upstream}} \\ & {\text{ = 1hr 15m = 1}}\frac{1}{4}hrs = \frac{5}{4}hrs \\ & {\text{Total time taken to cover 100 miles}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{5}{6} + \frac{5}{4}} \right)hrs = \frac{{25}}{{12}}hrs \\ & \therefore {\text{Average speed }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{100}}{{\left( {\frac{{25}}{{12}}} \right)}}mph \\ & = \left( {\frac{{100 \times 12}}{{25}}} \right)mph \\ & = 48mph. \end{aligned}$$

q: A boat travels 24 km upstream in 6 hours and 20 km downstream in 4 hours. Then the speed of boat in still water and the speed of current are respectively.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Upstream speed, U}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{24}}{6} = 4\,km/h \\ & {\text{Downstream speed , D}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{20}}{4} = 5\,km/h \\ & {\text{Speed of boat in still water , }}x \\ & = \frac{{{\text{D + U}}}}{2} = \frac{9}{2} = 4.5\,km/h \\ & {\text{Speed of water current, }}y \\ & = \frac{{{\text{D - U}}}}{2} = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5\,km/h \end{aligned}$$

q: A man can row 6 km/hr in still water. If the speed of the current is 2 km/hr he takes 4 hours more in upstream than the downstream. The distance is?
s: Speed of man in still water, x = 6 km/h Speed of current, y = 2 km/h Let distance = M According to question Upstream time = Downstream time + 4 $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{M}{4} = \frac{M}{8} + 4 \\ & \frac{M}{4} = \frac{{M + 32}}{8} \\ & M = 32 \\ & \therefore {\text{Distance = 32 }}km \end{aligned}$$

q: The speed of a boat along the stream is 12 km/hr and against the stream is 8 km/hr. The time taken by the boat to sail 24 km in still water is?
s: Speed of downstream D = 12 km/h Speed of upstream U = 8 km/h Speed of boat in still water $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{D + U}}{2} \\ & = \frac{{20}}{2} \\ & = 10\,km/h \end{aligned}$$ Time taken by the boat in still water $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{24\,km}}{{10\,km/hr}} \\ & = 2.4\,{\text{hours}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A motorboat in still water travels at a speed of 36 km/hr. It goes 56 km upstream in 1 hour 45 monutes. The time taken by it to cover the same distance down the stream will be-
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed upstream}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{56}}{{1\frac{3}{4}}}} \right)km/hr \\ & = \left( {56 \times \frac{4}{7}} \right)km/hr \\ & = 32km/hr \\ & {\text{let speed downstream be }}x{\text{ km/hr}}{\text{.}} \\ & {\text{Then speed of boat in still water }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{1}{2}\left( {x + 32} \right)km/hr \\ & \therefore {\text{ }}\frac{1}{2}\left( {x + 32} \right) = 36\,\,\, \Rightarrow x = 40 \\ & {\text{Hence , required time}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{{50}}{{40}}} \right)hrs \\ & = 1\frac{2}{5}hrs \\ & = 1\,{\text{hour}}\,24\operatorname{minutes} \end{aligned}$$

q: P, Q and R are three towns on a river which flows uniformly. Q is equidistant from P and R. I row from P to Q and back in 10 hours and I can row from P to R in 4 hours. Compare the speed of my boat in still water with that of the river.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let PQ = QR = }}x{\text{ }}km \\ & {\text{let speed downstream }} \\ & {\text{ = }}a{\text{ }}km/hr \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, \to \,\,{\text{downstream}} \to \\ & {\text{P}}\overline {\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,x\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Q}}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,y\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,} \,{\text{R}}\,\,\,\, \\ & {\text{and speed upstream }} \\ & {\text{ = }}b{\text{ }}km/hr{\text{ }} \\ & {\text{then, }}\frac{x}{a} + \frac{x}{b} = 10 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{10ab}}{{a + b}} \\ & {\text{and }}\frac{{2x}}{a} = 4 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{4a}}{2} = 2a \\ & {\text{from (i) and (ii) we have:}} \\ & 2a = \frac{{10ab}}{{a + b}} \\ & \Rightarrow 5b = a + b \\ & \Rightarrow a = 4b \\ & {\text{Required ratio }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{{\text{Speed in still water}}}}{{{\text{Speed of river}}}} \\ & = \frac{{\frac{1}{2}\left( {a + b} \right)}}{{\frac{1}{2}\left( {a - b} \right)}} \\ & = \frac{{\left( {a + b} \right)}}{{\left( {a - b} \right)}} \\ & = \frac{{4b + b}}{{4b - b}} \\ & = \frac{5}{3} \end{aligned}$$

q: A boat moves downstream at the rate of 1 km in $${\text{7}}\frac{1}{2}$$ minutes and upstream at the rate of 5 km an hour. What is the speed of the boat in the still water?
s: Rate downstream of boat $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{1}{{\frac{{15}}{{2 \times 60}}}}} \right)\,{\text{kmph}} \\ & = \frac{{2 \times 60}}{{15}}\,{\text{kmph}} \\ & = 8\,{\text{kmph}} \end{aligned}$$ Rate downstream of boat = 5 kmph Speed of boat in still water = $$\frac{1}{2}$$ (Rate downstream + Rate upstream) $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{2}\left( {8 + 5} \right) \\ & = \frac{{13}}{2} \\ & = 6\frac{1}{2}\,{\text{kmph}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A boat takes half time in moving a certain distance downstream than upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water and that of the current is?
s: Let the speed of boat in still water = x km/hr, and Speed of current = y km/hr Rate downstream = (x + y) km/hr, and Rate upstream = (x – y) km/hr Distance = Speed × Time $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \left( {x - y} \right) \times 2t = \left( {x + y} \right) \times t \\ & \Rightarrow 2x - 2y = x + y \\ & \Rightarrow 2x - x = 2y + y \\ & \Rightarrow x = 3y \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{x}{y} = \frac{3}{1} = 3:1 \end{aligned}$$ Alternate Solution : $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{According to Question}} \\ & {\text{Downstream Speed}} = x + y \\ & {\text{Upstream Speed}} = x - y \\ & {\text{Speed}} = \frac{{{\text{Distance}}}}{{{\text{Time}}}} \\ & \therefore x + y = \frac{D}{T}\, . . . . .\,\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & \,\,\,\,x - y = \frac{D}{{2T}}\,. . . . .\,\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & {\text{Solve equation}}\left( {\text{i}} \right){\text{ and }}\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & x = \frac{{3D}}{{4T}},\,\,\,\,y = \frac{D}{{4T}} \\ & \therefore \frac{x}{y} = \frac{{3D}}{{4T}} \times \frac{{4T}}{D} \\ & \,\,\,\,\frac{x}{y} = \frac{3}{1} \\ & \,\,\,\,x:y = 3:1 \end{aligned}$$

q: A man rows 12 km in 5 hours against the stream and the speed of current being 4 kmph. What time will be taken by him to row 15 km with the stream?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{According to question,}} \\ & {\text{Speed of current }}y = {\text{ }}4{\text{ }}km/h \\ & {\text{Distance = }}12{\text{ }}km \\ & {\text{Speed in upstream }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {x - y} \right)km/hr. \\ & {\text{Here }}x{\text{ is speed of boat in still water}} \\ & \,{\text{ = }}\frac{{{\text{Distance}}}}{{{\text{Time}}}} \\ & x - 4 = \frac{{12}}{5} \\ & 5x - 20 = 12 \\ & 5x = 32 \\ & x = 6.4\,km/hr \\ & {\text{Speed in downstream }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {x + y} \right) = 6.4 + 4 \\ & = 10.4\,km/h \\ & \therefore {\text{Time = }}\frac{{{\text{Distance}}}}{{{\text{Speed }}}} \\ & {\text{Time = }}\frac{{15}}{{10.4}} = \frac{{150}}{{104}} \\ & = 1\,{\text{hour}}\,\,26\frac{7}{{13}}\,\,{\text{minutes}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The speed of a boat downstream is 15 km/hr and the speed of current is 3 km/hr. Find the total time taken by the boat to cover 15 km upstream and 15 km downstream.
s: Given, Speed of boat in downstream = 15 km/hr Speed of current = 3 km/hr Speed of boat in still water = 12 km/h Time taken at upstream $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{15}}{{12 - 3}} \\ & = \frac{{15}}{9}{\text{hr}} \\ & = 1\,{\text{hour}}\,40\,{\text{minutes}} \end{aligned}$$ Time taken at downstream $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{15}}{{12 + 3}} \\ & = \frac{{15}}{{15}}{\text{hr}} \\ & = 1\,{\text{hour}}\, \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Total time = 2 hours 40 minutes

q: The speed of a boat in still water is 10 km/hr. If it can travel 26 km downstream and 14 km upstream at the same time, the speed of the stream is-
s: Let the speed of the stream be x km/hr Then speed downstream = (10 + x) km/hr Speed upstream $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = }}\left( {10 - x} \right)km/hr \\ & \therefore \frac{{26}}{{\left( {10 + x} \right)}} = \frac{{14}}{{\left( {10 - x} \right)}} \\ & \Rightarrow 260 - 26x = 140 + 14x \\ & \Rightarrow 40x = 120 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 3\,km/hr \end{aligned}$$

q: A man row to a place 48 km distant and back on 14 hours text. He finds that he can row 4 km with the stream in the same time as 3 km against the stream. The rate of the stream is?
s: Suppose he moves 4 km downstream in x hours. Then, Speed downstream $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{4}{x}} \right)km/hr \\ & {\text{Speed upstream}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {\frac{3}{x}} \right)km/hr \\ & \therefore \frac{{48}}{{\left( {\frac{3}{x}} \right)}} + \frac{{48}}{{\left( {\frac{4}{x}} \right)}} = 14\,\,\,or\,\,\,x = \frac{1}{2} \\ & So,\,{\text{Speed downstream}} \\ & {\text{ = 8 }}km/hr \\ & {\text{Speed uptream = 6 }}km/hr \\ & {\text{Rate of the stream}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{1}{2}\left( {8 - 6} \right)km/hr \\ & = 1\,km/hr \end{aligned}$$

q: Speed of a along and against the current are 14 kms/hr and 8 kms/hr respectively. The speed of the current is?
s: S + W = 14 . . . . . . (i) S - W = 8 . . . . . . . .(ii) _________________ from equation (i) & (ii) S = 11 km/hr, W = 3 km/hr Speed of current = 3 km/hr

q: If the speed of a boat in still water is 20km/hr and the speed of the current is 5km, then the time taken by the boat to travel 100 km with the current is?
s: Relative speed = 20 + 5 = 25 km/hr Time = $$\frac{{100}}{{25}}$$ = 4 hours

q: A man takes 2.2 times as long to row a distance upstream as to row the same distance downstream. If he can row 55 km downstream in 2 hour 30 minutes, what is the speed of the boat in the still water?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed of the boat in downstream }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{55}}{{2.5}} = \frac{{55 \times 10}}{{25}} = 22\,km/hr \\ & {\text{Then, speed of the boat in upstream}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{22}}{{2.2}} = \frac{{22 \times 10}}{{22}} = 10\,km/hr \\ & \therefore {\text{Speed of the boat in still water}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{22 + 10}}{2} = 16\,km/hr \end{aligned}$$

q: The speed of the boat in still water is 5 times that of current, it takes 1.1 hour to row to point B from point A downstream. The distance between point A and point B is 13.2 km. How much distance (in km) will it cover in 312 minutes upstrem?
s: Let the speed of the current be x kmph Then speed of the boat in still water = 5x $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{Downstream speed}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {5x + x} \right) = 6x\,kmph \\ & {\text{Upstream speed}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {5x - x} \right) = 4x\,kmph \\ & {\text{Now, }} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{13}}{\text{.2km}}\,\,\,\, \\ & {\text{A}}\overline {\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,} {\text{B}} \\ & {\text{According to question,}} \\ & {\text{1}}{\text{.1}} \times {\text{6}}x = 13.2 \\ & \Rightarrow 6.6x = 13.2 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{13.2}}{{6.6}} \\ & \therefore x = 2\,kmph \\ & \therefore {\text{Upstream speed}} \\ & {\text{ = 4}}x = 4 \times 2 = 8\,kmph \\ & \therefore {\text{312 minutes}}\, \\ & = 5\frac{1}{5}\,hours \\ & = \frac{{26}}{5}\,hours \\ & \therefore {\text{Required distance travelled upstream}} \\ & {\text{ = Speed }} \times {\text{Time}} \\ & {\text{ = 8}} \times \frac{{26}}{5} = 41.6\,km \end{aligned}$$

q: A boat can tarvel 36 km upstream in 5 hours. If the speed of the stream is 2.4 kmph, how much time will the boat take to cover a distance of 78 km downstream?(in hours)
s: Distance covered by a boat in 5 hours = 36 km Rate upstream of boat = $$\frac{{36}}{5}$$ = 7.2 kmph Speed of the stream = 2.4 kmph ∴ Speed of the boat in still water = (7.2 + 2.4) kmph = 9.6 kmph ∴ Rate downstream of the boat = (9.6 + 2.4) kmph = 12 kmph ∴ Time taken in covering 78 km distance = $$\frac{{78}}{{12}}$$ = 6.5 hours

q: A man can row upstream at 12km/hr and downstream at 18 km/hr. The man rowing speed in still water is?
s: Speed of boat in still water = $$\frac{{x + y}}{2}$$ Where (x = downstream speed) and (y = upstream speed) ∴ Boat's speed $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = }}\frac{{18 + 12}}{2} \\ & = \frac{{30}}{2} \\ & = 15\,km/hr \end{aligned}$$

q: On a river , Q is the mid - point between two points P and R on the same bank of the river. A boat can go from P to Q and back in 12 hours, and from P to R in 16 hours 40 minutes. How long would it take to go from R to P?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{P - - - - - - - - - - }}\mathop {\text{ - }}\limits_{\text{Q}} {\text{ - - - - - - - - - - R}} \\ & {\text{ < - - - - - - - 16}}{\text{.40 - - - - - - - > }} \\ & \because {\text{Time required travelling from P to R}} \\ & {\text{ = 16H 40M}} \\ & \because {\text{PQ = QR}}\left( {\because {\text{Q is mid point}}} \right){\text{ }} \\ & {\text{Required time to travel PQ}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{1}{2}\left( {{\text{16H 40M}}} \right) = \,\,{\text{8H 20M}} \\ & {\text{total required time from}} \\ & {\text{P to Q + Q to P = 12H}} \\ & {\text{ = 8H 20M + Q to P = 12H}} \\ & {\text{Time Q to P}} \\ & {\text{ = 12H - 8H 20M}} \\ & {\text{ = 3H 40M}} \\ & \because \overrightarrow {{\text{QP}}} {\text{ = }}\frac{1}{2}\overrightarrow {{\text{RP}}} {\text{ }}\,\,\left( {{\text{Distance}}} \right) \\ & \therefore {\text{Required time to }}\overrightarrow {{\text{RP}}} {\text{ }} \\ & {\text{ = 2}} \times \left[ {\overrightarrow {{\text{QP}}} } \right] \\ & {\text{ = 2}}\left[ {3{\text{H 40M}}} \right]{\text{ }} \\ & {\text{ = 7 H 20M}} \\ & {\text{ = 7}}\frac{1}{3}{\text{hr}}{\text{ }} \end{aligned}$$

q: A boat can row 35 km, upstream in 7 hours and the same distance downstream in 5 hours. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the boat in still water?
s: Speed of boat in upstream = $$\frac{{35}}{7}$$ = 5 km/hr Speed of boat in downstream = $$\frac{{35}}{5}$$ = 7 km/hr Let the speed of boat x and speed of stream be y Now, x - y = 5 x + y = 7 $$\overline {\,2{\text{x}} = 12\,}$$ ∴ x = 6 km/hr

q: A man rows to a place 48 km distant and comes back in 14 hours. He finds that he can row 4 km with the stream in the same time as 3 km against the stream. The speed of the stream is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let, speed of boat}} = x \\ & {\text{Speed of stream}} = y \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{48}}{{x + y}} + \frac{{48}}{{x - y}} = 14\,.\,.\,.\,.\,.\,\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & {\text{and, }}\frac{4}{{x + y}} = \frac{3}{{x - y}} \\ & \frac{{x - y}}{{x + y}} = \frac{3}{4} = \frac{6}{8} \\ & {\text{From equation }}\left( {\text{i}} \right), \\ & \frac{{48}}{8} + \frac{{48}}{6} = 14 \\ & 14 = 14\,\,\,\left( {{\text{Satisfied}}} \right) \\ & {\text{So, }}x - y = 6 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,x + y = 8 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\overline {\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,y = 1\,\,} {\text{km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$

q: A motorboat goes 24 km in 2 hour along the stream and 10 km in 1 hour against the stream. The speed of the motorboat in kilometres per hour, is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{B}} + {\text{W}} = 12{\text{ km/h}} \\ & {\text{B}} - {\text{W}} = 10{\text{ km/h}} \\ & \overline {\,{\text{B}} = \frac{{22}}{2} = 11{\text{ km/h}}\,} \end{aligned}$$

q: A boat moves 25 km upstream and 39 km downstream in 8 hours. It travels 35 km upstream and 52 km downstream in 11 hours. What is the speed of the stream if it travels at a uniform speed?
s: Let speed of boat is x and stream is y km/hr According to the question $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{25}}{{x - y}} + \frac{{39}}{{x + y}} = 8 \\ & \frac{{35}}{{x - y}} + \frac{{52}}{{x + y}} = 11 \end{aligned}$$ By hit and trail method x = 9, y = 4 it satisfy the both equations Speed of stream = 4 km/hr

q: A boat can cover a distance of 56 km downstream in 3.5 hours. The ratio of the boat in still water and the speed of stream is 3 : 1. How much time (in hours) will the boat take to cover a distance of 41.6 km downstream?
s: Speed of boat in downstream $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{56}}{{3.5}} \\ & = \frac{{56}}{7} \times 2 \\ & = 16{\text{ km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Required time $$= \frac{{41.6}}{{16}} = 2.6{\text{ hrs}}$$

q: A man rows a boat a certain distance downstream in 9 hours, while it takes 18 hours to row the same distance upstream. How many hours will it take him to row $$\frac{3}{5}$$ of the same distance in still water?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Speed of boat}} = x \\ & {\text{Speed of stream}} = y \\ & {\text{Distance}} = 9\left( {x + y} \right) = 18\left( {x - y} \right) \\ & x + y = 2x - 2y \\ & x = 3y \\ & {\text{Distance}} = 9\left( {x + y} \right) \\ & = 9\left( {3y + y} \right) \\ & = 36y \\ & 36y \times \frac{3}{5} = t \times x \\ & 36y \times \frac{3}{5} = t \times 3y \\ & t = \frac{{36}}{5} = 7.2 \end{aligned}$$

q: Two boat are travelling with speed of 36 km/hr and 54 km/hr respectively towards each other. What is the distance (in metres) between the two boats one second before they collide?
s: Distance Relative Speed = Time Distance = 36 + 54 × 1 = 90 × 5 18 × 1 km/hr → × 5 18 m/sec = 25 metre

q: A motor boat can travel 40 km downstream and 30 km upstream in 10 hours. It can travel 80 km downstream and 40 km upstream in 15 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Motor boat}} \\ & \frac{{40}}{{x + y}} + \frac{{30}}{{x - y}} = 10\,.\,.\,.\,.\,.\,\left( 1 \right) \\ & \frac{{80}}{{x + y}} + \frac{{40}}{{x - y}} = 15\,.\,.\,.\,.\,.\,\left( 2 \right) \\ & \frac{{20}}{{x - y}} = 5 \\ & x - y = 4\,.\,.\,.\,.\,.\,\left( 3 \right) \\ & {\text{From equation }}\left( 2 \right),\,\frac{{80}}{{x + y}} + 10 = 15 \\ & x + y = 16\,.\,.\,.\,.\,.\,\left( 4 \right) \\ & {\text{From equation }}\left( 3 \right)\,{\text{and }}\left( 4 \right) \\ & x = 10,\,y = 6 \\ & {\text{Speed of motor boat}} = 10\,{\text{Answer}} \\ & \\ & {\bf{Alternate\, Solution}} \\ & \left( {40 + 30} \right) - \left( {80 + 40} \right) = \left( {10 - 15} \right){\text{hr}} \\ & 5\,{\text{hr}} \to {\text{50 km}} \\ & 1\,{\text{hr}} \to 1{\text{0 km}} \\ & {\text{Speed }} = 1{\text{0 km/hr}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The speed of a boat in still water is 15 km/h, and the speed of the current is 5 km/h. In how much time (in hours) will the boat travel a distance of 60 km upstream and the same distance downstream?
s: Speed of boat in still water = 15 km/hr Speed of stream = 5 km/hr Total time of upstream and downstream $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{60}}{{15 - 5}} + \frac{{60}}{{15 + 5}} \\ & = 6 + 3 \\ & = 9{\text{ hr}} \end{aligned}$$

A swimmer swims from a point P against the current for 6 min and then swims back along the current for next 6 min and reaches at a point Q. If the distance between P and Q is 120 m then the speed of the current (in km/h) is:
s: Understanding the Problem: Imagine a swimmer swimming in a river. The river's current pushes the swimmer, affecting their speed. The swimmer swims against the current (meaning the current slows them down) for 6 minutes, then turns around and swims with the current (the current speeds them up) for another 6 minutes. The total distance covered during this time is 120 meters. We need to find the speed of the river's current. Breaking it Down: Let's say the swimmer's speed in still water is 'x' m/min and the speed of the current is 'y' m/min. When swimming against the current, the effective speed is (x - y) m/min (because the current slows them down). When swimming with the current, the effective speed is (x + y) m/min (because the current helps them). Calculations: Distance covered against the current = (x - y) * 6 minutes Distance covered with the current = (x + y) * 6 minutes The difference between these two distances is 120 meters (the distance between points P and Q): [(x + y) * 6] - [(x - y) * 6] = 120 Simplifying this equation, we get: 6x + 6y - 6x + 6y = 120 12y = 120 y = 10 m/min Converting to km/h: We have the speed of the current as 10 m/min. To convert this to km/h, we need to multiply by 60 (minutes in an hour) and divide by 1000 (meters in a kilometer): (10 m/min) * (60 min/hour) / (1000 m/km) = 0.6 km/h Therefore, the speed of the current is 0.6 km/h. The correct option is D.

q: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the current is 6 km/h. In how much time (in hours) will the boat travel a distance of 90 km upstream and the same distance downstream?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{90}}{{{\text{Boat}} - {\text{Stream}}}} + \frac{{90}}{{{\text{Boat}} + {\text{Stream}}}} = {\text{Time}} \\ & \frac{{90}}{{12}} + \frac{{90}}{{24}} = {\text{Time}} \\ & {\text{Time}} = \frac{{270}}{{24}} = \frac{{45}}{4} = 11\frac{1}{4} \end{aligned}$$

q: A boat can go 5 km upstream and $$7\frac{1}{2}$$ km downstream in 45 minutes. If can also go 5 km downstream and 2.5 km upstream in 25 minutes. How much time (in minutes) will it take to go 6 km upstream?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{5}{{x - y}} + \frac{{15}}{{2\left( {x + y} \right)}} = \frac{3}{4}{\text{hr }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & \frac{{2.5 \times 2}}{{x - y}} + \frac{{5 \times 2}}{{x + y}} = \frac{{5 \times 2}}{{12}}{\text{hr }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}{\text{. }}\left( {{\text{ii}}} \right) \\ & \frac{5}{{2\left( {x + y} \right)}} = \frac{1}{{12}} \\ & x + y = 30 \\ & {\text{Put }}x + y = 30{\text{ in equation }}\left( {\text{i}} \right) \\ & \frac{5}{{x - y}} + \frac{{15}}{{2 \times 30}} = \frac{3}{4} \\ & \frac{5}{{x - y}} = \frac{1}{2} \\ & x - y = 10 \\ & {\text{Now,}} \\ & \,x + y = 30 \\ & \underline {\,x - y = 10\,} \\ & x = 20 \\ & y = 10 \\ & \frac{{6\,{\text{km}}}}{{x - y}} = \frac{6}{{10}} \times 60 = 36\min \end{aligned}$$
